## Why this round exists

QA spread is MEASURED from banked #1739 rollouts (TriviaQA reliability 0.940, NQ-Open 0.934,
SimpleQA 0.035 mean / 91% zero-pile — dropped). Math and code spread for
Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct are UNMEASURED: only published aggregates under other protocols exist,
and the pooled code figure (0.504–0.535, recomputed by problem-count weighting over HumanEval
84.8 / MBPP 79.2 / BigCodeBench-full 46.1 Complete or 37.6 Instruct / LiveCodeBench 28.7) derives
its spread substantially from a mixture ACROSS benchmarks rather than demonstrated WITHIN-benchmark
dispersion — the #2388 risk-10 benchmark-identity confound. This pilot measures the real thing.

## Scope

200 items × K=5 rollouts × 3 surfaces (math, MCQ, code) at the production protocol: Qwen chat
template, temperature 1.0, zero-shot, sampled (not greedy). Per-benchmark reporting, never pooled
— separating within-benchmark dispersion from the mixture artifact is the whole point.

Output per benchmark: mean, SD(y), SD(true rate), reliability and ceiling rho via the
beta-binomial decomposition Var(p) = Var(y) - mean(y(1-y))/(K-1), plus the zero-pile / one-pile
fractions. Admissibility rule (pre-registered): a pool is admissible while NEITHER extreme
exceeds ~90% — the shape that disqualified SimpleQA.

[spread-pilot] COMPLETE — 4 of 5 benchmarks admissible; bigcodebench harness-limited

Zero-shot per-item correctness spread for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct at the production protocol
(K=5 rollouts, temperature 1.0, top_p 1.0, vLLM seed 2388, per-request seed deliberately
unset so the K draws are independent). This answers the pre-registration question "is the
correctness DV usefully spread on each surface, or does it saturate?" before the full
experiment commits GPU.

## Reading the columns

- `mean` — fraction of rollouts correct, averaged over items.
- `SD(p)` — the spread of TRUE per-item correctness rates, after subtracting the
  sampling noise that K=5 draws contribute. `SD(y)` (raw) is inflated by that noise.
  Beta-binomial decomposition: `Var(p) = Var(y) - mean(y(1-y))/(K-1)`.
- `reliab` — share of the observed between-item spread that is real signal rather than
  K=5 sampling noise. `Var(p)/Var(y)`.
- `ceil` — `sqrt(reliab)`: the highest correlation ANY predictor could reach against this
  K=5-estimated label. A predictor scoring 0.6 against a ceiling of 0.94 is at 64% of
  what is attainable, not at 60% of perfect.
- `zero` / `one` — share of items the model got wrong on all 5 draws / right on all 5.
  These are the "piles". Admissibility rule: neither pile above ~90%.
- `unpars` — completions that could not be parsed into an answer at all. Recorded
  separately, never coerced to "incorrect" (drop-never-coerce).
- `identical` — share of items where all K completions were byte-identical. A degenerate
  sampler would push this to 100% and manufacture fake bimodality.

## Results

| benchmark | n | mean | SD(p) | reliab | ceil | zero | one | unpars | identical | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| humaneval | 164 | 0.815 | 0.316 | 0.906 | 0.952 | 8.5% | 69.5% | 0.0% | 14.6% | ADMISSIBLE |
| math500 | 200 | 0.782 | 0.320 | 0.882 | 0.939 | 8.5% | 64.0% | 0.0% | 0.0% | ADMISSIBLE |
| mbpp | 150 | 0.673 | 0.415 | 0.946 | 0.972 | 22.0% | 58.0% | 0.0% | 8.0% | ADMISSIBLE |
| mmlu_pro | 191 | 0.586 | 0.373 | 0.870 | 0.933 | 20.4% | 36.6% | 1.5% | 0.0% | ADMISSIBLE |
| bigcodebench | 149 | 0.165 | 0.309 | 0.918 | 0.958 | 73.2% | 9.4% | 0.1% | 0.0% | INCONCLUSIVE |

Cap-hit fraction was 0.000% on every benchmark except mmlu_pro (1.900%), so truncation is
not manufacturing failures. Reliability 0.87-0.95 across the board means K=5 is enough:
the between-item spread is dominated by real item-to-item difficulty, not by rollout noise.

## Code-harness positive control — REQUIRED, and it caught one

Each code benchmark's OWN reference solution was pushed through the SAME
`extract_code` -> `verify_code` path the pilot used, ON THE POD (25 items per benchmark).
A missing import on the pod would fail every item and manufacture a FALSE zero-pile that
reads as "the model got it wrong".

| benchmark | canonical pass rate | composition | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| humaneval | 25/25 = 1.000 | `prompt + canonical_solution` | HARNESS-OK |
| mbpp | 25/25 = 1.000 | `code` | HARNESS-OK |
| bigcodebench | 13/25 = 0.520 | `code_prompt + canonical_solution` | HARNESS-SUSPECT |

BigCodeBench's failures are a POD ENVIRONMENT GAP, not a harness-logic bug and not model
error. Named causes, read from the failing runs' stderr: `ModuleNotFoundError: sklearn`
(bcb-38), `matplotlib` (bcb-48, bcb-86), `flask` (bcb-81). The wrapper passes every item
whose libraries are present; `canonical_only` scores 0/25, confirming `code_prompt` is the
required prefix. BigCodeBench spans 139 libraries by design and needs its official pinned
environment.

Therefore **bigcodebench's mean=0.165 / zero-pile=73.2% is NOT a valid model measurement**
and is not counted toward admissibility. Including BigCodeBench in the full experiment
requires provisioning its official dependency set first; that is a decision for the plan,
not a pilot finding.

## Verdict

PASS. All four harness-verified benchmarks are admissible, covering every surface the
experiment needs:

- math -> math500 (ADMISSIBLE)
- MCQ -> mmlu_pro (ADMISSIBLE)
- code -> humaneval + mbpp (ADMISSIBLE, both harness-verified 25/25)
- QA -> already established from banked #1739 data (reliability 0.93-0.94)

No evidence for switching to a stronger model: nothing saturates, and the two piles stay
far below the ~90% bar on every admissible benchmark.

Caveat carried forward: humaneval's 14.6% all-K-identical rate (vs 0.0% on math/MCQ) means
a meaningful minority of HumanEval items produce one deterministic completion under
sampling, so their per-item rate is 0 or 1 by construction rather than by difficulty. mbpp
(8.0%) is intermediate. Not disqualifying — reliability is 0.906/0.946 — but the full
experiment should report this per-benchmark rather than pool it away.

A 2026 paper fits supervised linear probes on pre-generation activations regressing the
K-rollout expected success rate on math and code — the same rate target this task
formalizes, at K=5 for one model family. In-domain it reaches binary AUROC 0.68-0.85 on
math and 0.90-0.91 on code pass-at-5, and it explicitly beats question-length and TF-IDF
surface baselines.

This is the closest prior formalization that exists and the plan's method-delta section
has to name it. It does not sink the task: what that paper leaves untouched is our model,
matched-label-budget comparisons, cross-surface transfer (its own stated limitation), and
any map-based prior. But a plan whose prior-work section does not mention it would be
overclaiming novelty on the direct arm.

## Finding 2 — the body's per-surface novelty read was pointed at the wrong surface

The body asserts recall QA is settled while math and code are genuinely open. The review
finds that directionally right on the QA-versus-code maturity axis but wrong on which
surface is emptiest. Math is MORE established than assumed — in-domain pre-generation
probes exist, and what actually fails there is transfer INTO math and any privileged
self-knowledge advantage. Code is established in two independent settings, though each is
single-model and the contrastive-direction variant is configuration-fragile.

The genuinely empty surface is multiple choice. No pre-generation last-prompt-token
correctness probe on MMLU-Pro or plain MMLU was found anywhere; the state of the art there
is post-generation. So the per-surface novelty of the direct hypothesis concentrates in
MCQ, which is also the surface whose chain-of-thought pooling fork the planner just
resolved. That coincidence is worth the planner's attention.

## Finding 3 — the map-as-prior hypothesis has no published analogue

Repeated targeted queries plus citation snowballing surfaced nothing that fits a learned
map between a question representation and an answer representation on unjudged pairs and
uses it as a prior to cut a labeled probe's budget. The near relatives each miss a limb:
the present-to-future state maps are interpretability and speculative-decoding devices
with no correctness target and no label-budget analysis; the sampling-derived-supervision
work substitutes labels by a different mechanism entirely; the cross-model transfer work
does domain adaptation rather than a representation map; the consistency-search line needs
zero labels but is not a map.

The empty result is itself a reportable finding, and it means this task's headline novelty
sits where the body said it does. The review also supplies the anchors the map arm has to
beat: a 25-label point recovering 90 percent of full-data performance, and a
160-to-2,560-label curve.

## Finding 4 — the confound literature validates controls the plan already carries

Question-identity leakage inflates random-split probe scores badly enough that
within-question performance collapses to chance under grouped evaluation, which makes the
plan's group-level folds mandatory rather than stylistic. On recall QA the internal signal
is substantially knowledge recall rather than truthfulness. Self-versus-external probe
advantage appears only on disagreement subsets, which promotes the external-assessor
baseline from decoration to load-bearing. Output-confidence baselines can beat activation
probes on raw discrimination, so the honest claim is about temporal position rather than
raw score. Each of these maps onto a control the plan already has; the review's
contribution is telling us which ones carry the weight.

[critic-finding VERIFIED — most serious of the batch] The fixed unlabeled-pool size cannot coexist with the disjointness requirement and the label grid. Code cannot satisfy it at all.

consistency checker — did not surface it. This is what an adversarial ensemble is for.

## The collision

The composition factor registers three cells at a FIXED unlabeled-pool size of 8,000 pairs,
with the target-surface portion drawn DISJOINT from the readout's labeled contexts and from
every evaluation rung. The label sweep runs to 8,000 and to full-label. Group splits are
70/10/20.

Those three commitments are jointly unsatisfiable. Arithmetic, computed directly from the
plan's own per-surface totals:

| surface | pool total | train at 70% | largest label budget that leaves a disjoint 8,000-pair map pool |
|---|---|---|---|
| QA | 16,000 | 11,200 | 3,200 |
| math | 12,500 | 8,750 | 750 |
| multiple-choice | 12,032 | 8,422 | 422 |
| code | 6,027 pre-dedup | 4,218 | none — impossible |

The registered grid runs {250, 500, 1k, 2k, 4k, 8k, full}. So on math only the two smallest
budgets are feasible beside a full-size disjoint pool; on multiple-choice only the smallest;
on code the target-only cell cannot exist at any budget, because the entire pre-deduplication
pool is smaller than the required pool size before any split is taken.

## Why it is conclusion-changing rather than a sizing detail

It lands on both headline hypotheses at once. The label-efficiency hypothesis needs the
matched-budget curves through the upper anchors; the composition hypothesis needs the pool
size held fixed across its three cells, since that is the entire reason the design replaces
rather than adds. As drafted, execution has only two ways to proceed, and both destroy a
headline: overlap the contexts, which routes the readout's own training contexts into the map
channel; or silently shrink the pool or the budget per cell, which voids the fixed-quantity
comparison the composition hypothesis rests on and breaks the matched-budget premise of the
efficiency curves.

The plan half-knew: its own rationale section concedes target-surface pools cap near 4,200
usable disjoint pairs on code, and never reconciles that against the 8,000 it registers three
cells at.

## The resolution the design already contains

The task body already contemplates both configurations. Strict disjointness is currently
primary, with the OVERLAPPING configuration run as a variant on the stated grounds that the
map never sees labels, so an overlapping pool leaks no label information and is the more
realistic deployment shape.

That inverts cleanly. Making the overlapping configuration PRIMARY for the composition cells
preserves the fixed pool size across all four surfaces and keeps the full label grid, with
strict disjointness retained as the variant wherever it is actually feasible. The alternative
is to register a smaller common pool size that every surface can satisfy disjointly — bounded
by code's roughly 4,200, so realistically nearer 3,000 — and to state the reduced size as the
registered value everywhere rather than letting it drift per cell.

Either is defensible. What is not defensible is shipping three commitments that cannot all
hold, and discovering it when the code surface's target-only cell fails to populate.

The parent's dependent-variable builder defines the `dv` field as the FABRICATION fraction —

The reused fits entrypoint reads exactly that field when it loads a dependent-variable JSON.

fraction AGREE on 642 and DIFFER on 22,546. A representative row carries a fabrication value
of 0.8 against a correctness value of 0.0 — not a rounding difference, an unrelated quantity.

## What would have happened

The QA surface is the plan's entire Phase 0 — the leg that is free because the labels are
already banked, and the leg that carries the knowledge-versus-persona hypothesis. Run as
drafted, every QA number would have been a fabrication-rate readout. The
knowledge-versus-persona comparison would have compared a disposition property against other
disposition properties, which is precisely the confusion this task was created to resolve. It
would have produced a confident, internally consistent, entirely wrong result on the surface
with the most banked data behind it.

## How it got this far — three verification passes each stopped one step short

The task body asserted that the correctness dependent variable already exists in that file
and that the fits entrypoint accepts a dependent-variable-JSON override, concluding the
Phase 0 ladder is a dependent-variable swap over existing arms. Both individual premises are
TRUE: the file does carry a correctness fraction, and the script does accept the override
flag. The inference between them is false, because the flag's loader binds to a different
field inside the file.

The clarifier pass — mine — verified the flag exists at its cited line and that the file
carries the correctness field, then wrote that Phase 0 is genuinely a dependent-variable swap.
That conclusion was wrong and I am correcting it here: existence of a flag and existence of a
field do not establish that the flag consumes that field.

The Phase 1.5 fact-check verified the flag, counted the file's rows at full grain, and
confirmed the correctness fraction is present on every row — all correct, and all silent on
which field the consumer reads.

Four reviewers before this twin looked at the plan and did not catch it either. The single
question none of the passes asked was: which field does the consumer actually read.

## Fix

Either materialize a correctness-specific dependent-variable file whose `dv` field carries the
correctness fraction, or add an explicit field-selector argument to the entrypoint and test
it. The test has to be adversarial: a fixture whose two fields hold deliberately different
values, asserting the requested one is what reaches the fit. A fixture where both fields agree
proves nothing — which is exactly how 642 agreeing rows could have masked this.

This class is not specific to one task: a plan claims reuse of a script plus an artifact, both
halves verify, and the FIELD BINDING between them is never checked. A mechanical verifier
could assert that a reuse claim naming a field also names the consumer line that reads it.

well-determined anchors the advantage has essentially evaporated: two behaviors within a
hundredth of zero, and sycophancy NEGATIVE.

## Why this is decisive rather than interesting

The knowledge-versus-persona hypothesis reads the correctness gap against the banked persona
gaps at matched anchors, and its registered kill criterion fires when the correctness gap's
interval sits at or below zero WHILE the banked persona gaps stay positive. At the
well-determined anchors the persona gaps are not positive. So the criterion cannot fire, and the
comparison is null-against-null with no contrast to detect.

This is a direct consequence of the fix applied one round earlier. Restricting the comparison to
well-determined anchors was the correct answer to the estimator-validity problem — five reviewers
converged on that defect and the restriction resolves it. But it relocated the comparison to the
label-rich end of the curve, where the parent's own effect has already decayed. The validity fix
and the contrast are in tension, and the band where the parent shows a real effect — 2,500 labels
— is precisely the under-determined regime the project bans on the parent's uncapped selector.

The hypothesis is caught between the two: the phenomenon it wants to compare against manifests
only where the numbers measuring it cannot be trusted.

## The resolution, and why it is now cheap

Recompute the parent's gaps at 2,500 labels through the capped selector, for the three behaviors,
and run the comparison there. That is the expensive option the previous revision declined — but
the estimate it was declined on was for the general case. Scoped to ONE budget and three
behaviors it is small: the plan's own measured basis puts the parent's readout group wall at
roughly forty-six seconds per twenty-eight-layer batched group at that budget, against a hundred
and forty at the largest. This is tens of minutes of compute, not hours.

It also does not touch the live parent session: recomputing means RUNNING fits over banked
activations into a new output path with the cap passed explicitly. Nothing about the parent's
module changes, and its in-flight jobs are unaffected.

The alternatives are worse. Accepting the comparison as null-against-null means shipping a
hypothesis that cannot fire, which the plan would then have to declare untestable as designed.
Dropping the hypothesis entirely discards the sharpest read in the task — it is the whole reason
correctness was chosen as a knowledge property to contrast against dispositions.

Neither the plan, nor five reviewers across two rounds, nor my own three verification passes
caught this, because every one of them reasoned about the estimator and none of them looked at
what the banked numbers actually contain at the anchors the fix selected. The round-2 alternatives
critic did not catch it either — it PREDICTED it from the label-efficiency prior and recommended
the check. Running the check is what settled it.

## Three constraints, not one

The 158 GB figure trips three separate project rules, and they bind differently:

maximum — which independently routes the consuming phase off the VM at plan time rather than
after a failure.

sequential staging is the simpler shape and matches the existing contract.

behavior; each behavior is atomic at its own size.

The plan pins the comparison's FILES, anchors and selector, but never pins what
